text:
alex: Quick question — prepping the SDK v2 docs + release. Need a final check on embeddings endpoint behavior so the docs don't promise anything wrong. TL;DR: what do we do for single-string vs list inputs, null/empty items, truncation semantics, and the exact vector shape returned?

maria: Short answers first: we accept single string and list (coerce single -> [string]); null -> treated as empty string; empty string not an error; truncation is model-configurable but we have a default char-limit fallback; vectors are model-dependent, we return a list of vectors matching input order.

cheng: +1 to that summary. For numbers: current default per-item char truncation cutoff is 50k chars unless a model override exists. Per-request item limit is 1024 items (we cap at that on the API gateway).

riley: FWIW we also do early-reject if request payload > 15MB after JSON encoding to protect running out of memory — that's enforced at edge. Docs should mention both the per-item char cap and the payload-size guard.

alex: Useful. A couple of followups: 1) If client sends ["foo", null, ""] what do we return exactly? 2) Do we preserve order and length even if some items are coerced/truncated? 3) What does each vector look like (flat array? typed)?

maria: 1) We return a vector for each input item in the same order. null -> coerced to "" internally, so you get an embedding for the empty string. 2) Yes preserved order/length — we never drop items. 3) Response is JSON: { "data": [ {"embedding": [f32,...]}, ... ] } — arrays of floats. We don't return typed arrays over the wire. Add: we include metadata at the top-level: model, usage.tokens, request_id.

cheng: To be super explicit for the docs: example request + response block might help.

alex: Can you paste a tiny example here I can copy into docs?

maria: Sure — example (trimmed):
```
POST /v1/embeddings
{
  "model": "rwd-embed-lite-1536",
  "input": ["hello", null, ""]
}

200 OK
{
  "model": "rwd-embed-lite-1536",
  "request_id": "req_abc123",
  "data": [
    {"embedding": [0.012, -0.034, ... ]},
    {"embedding": [0.000, 0.001, ... ]},
    {"embedding": [0.000, -0.002, ... ]}
  ]
}
```
Note: vectors are length 1536 for that model. Use ellipses in docs.

riley: Also call out numeric precision: we serialize as JSON numbers (32-bit float precision is fine), clients should parse as floats. No base64 encoding.

alex: Good. About truncation: do we append any sentinel or do we just cut? Users want to detect truncation sometimes to avoid silent data loss.

cheng: We currently just cut at the cutoff. No sentinel appended. BUT we do include a warnings array in the response if any input was truncated. Response shape: optional top-level "warnings": [ {"index": 2, "reason": "truncated", "orig_length": 120000, "truncated_to": 50000} ] — that helps programmatic detection. Docs should show that.

maria: Add that warnings may be absent if nothing was truncated. Also mention we only report the first truncation per request to keep response small (we don't list every single truncated item if >1000 truncated items). We instead set warnings.limit_exceeded=true in that case.

alex: Backcompat concern: old clients might send a single string in the body as raw "input": "foo" (not a list). We coerce, but should we log a deprecation header?

riley: We add an "x-deprecation-warning" response header for one year pointing them to change to list form. After that we'll drop coercion in a future major. Put that in the migration note.

cheng: One more: ordering and async batching — if backend shards reorder internally, we still map outputs back to original indices using an internal index field. So returned array order is guaranteed to match input order. Docs can say: "Order is preserved; if you need deterministic per-item IDs include your own id field in items."

alex: For per-item metadata, do we support passing objects like {"text":"...","id":"abc"}? Or only bare strings?

maria: We accept both. If you pass objects we look for "text" (or "input") and optional "id". If both present we echo back id in the corresponding data element: {"id":"abc","embedding": [...] }. If you pass just strings they get anonymous indices. Add snippet showing both styles.

alex: Great. Anything else I should highlight about rate limits or batch sizing?

riley: Recommend doc guidance: prefer batching up to 256 items per request for best latency/cost tradeoff — we accept up to 1024 but latency/backpressure increases. Also an ops note: large batches may be split server-side; include note that you may see multiple partial logs for a single request in traces.

maria: Also call out empty list behavior: POSTing input: [] returns data: [] (200) — not an error. That subtlety caused confusion before.

alex: Perfect. I'm going to add all this to the SDK v2 spec. One last ask: exact JSON field names for warnings and data must be stable. Can you confirm final canonical example for docs?

cheng: Use this canonical response shape in docs:
```
{
  "model": "<model-name>",
  "request_id": "<id>",
  "usage": {"input_chars": 1234},
  "warnings": [ {"index": 1, "reason": "truncated", "orig_length": 90000, "truncated_to": 50000} ],
  "data": [
    {"id": "optional-id", "embedding": [float, ...]},
    {"embedding": [float, ...]}
  ]
}
```
Use that verbatim.

maria: I'll drop a tiny PR to docs with examples and the migration note for single-string coercion + deprecation header.

alex: Thanks all — that'll unblock the release. :rocket:

ops-bot: Note: Edge guard triggered 2024-11-02T14:03Z — request payload size limit hit for a customer test — engineering aware.

riley: Filed followup issue #1024 to add a bin/cli stress test for large batches.

alex: Awesome — closing the loop here. If you see anything to change ping me in-thread.
